title: Best AI Resume Builders in 2027: 8 Tools Compared
summary: Simplify, Teal, Rezi, Jobscan, Kickresume, Enhancv and ChatGPT side by side: which one rewrites a CV for a specific job posting, which exports Word files, and what each costs as of November 2026.
body_markdown:
The best AI resume builder for most job seekers in 2027 is one that tailors your resume to each job description and then carries that version into the application, so you aren't rebuilding it for every posting. That's what my team built Simplify's resume builder to do, so it's first on this list. If you want something else, like design-heavy templates, a one-time price or a strict keyword checker, another tool on this list does that better, and I say which.


Before I started Simplify, I was a college student applying to over 200 positions in one cycle and tracking them in a spreadsheet. Most of what an AI resume builder does today is work job seekers used to do by hand: reading a posting, finding the skills it asks for and rewriting bullets to match. The good tools speed that up. They don't make up experience you don't have.


Disclosure first: we make Simplify. I checked every price below on each company's own pricing page on November 25, 2026, except Jobscan's, which sits behind a sign-in. Prices change, so treat them as a snapshot.

## How I ranked them


I asked five questions of each tool. Can the free plan produce a resume you'd actually send? Does the AI work from a specific job description, or does it write generic bullets? Will the file read cleanly in an applicant tracking system? Can you export the format employers ask for? And does the resume connect to the rest of your search, or do you copy it somewhere else afterward?


## 1. Simplify: best free AI resume builder for tailoring to each job


Simplify's[AI Resume Builder](https://simplify.jobs/resume-builder?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=best-ai-resume-builders-2027&utm_content=body-1) is free to build, edit and export, and it's the one tool here where the tailored resume goes straight into your applications. Start from your Simplify profile, import an existing resume or build section by section. The free plan includes four templates designed for ATS readability, an ATS Readiness Score with section-by-section feedback, and keyword matching against a job description you paste in, so you see which skills the posting asks for that your resume doesn't mention.


**Tailoring.** Paste the job description, check the missing keywords, and save a version for that job. With[Simplify+](https://simplify.jobs/plus?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=best-ai-resume-builders-2027&utm_content=body-2) , the AI suggests job-specific rewrites for your summary and bullets, and you can chat with it to edit. It works from the experience you've added, and every suggestion is yours to accept or change.


**Versions per job.** You can keep a separate version for each role and connect it to that job, so you know which resume you sent where. In the 30 days to November 24, 2026, about 25,000 people created about 120,000 resumes in the resume builder on Simplify, and about 90,000 of them (77%) were tied to a specific job posting.


**From resume to application.** The free[Copilot](https://simplify.jobs/copilot?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=best-ai-resume-builders-2027&utm_content=body-3) extension fills out applications on sites like Workday and Greenhouse with your resume and profile, and you review and submit. Each application lands in the free[Job Tracker](https://simplify.jobs/job-application-tracker?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=best-ai-resume-builders-2027&utm_content=body-4) , next to the resume version you used. If you'd rather not fill the forms at all,[Autopilot](https://simplify.jobs/ai-auto-apply?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=best-ai-resume-builders-2027&utm_content=body-5) can tailor your resume for a job you pick and submit the application on supported systems, including Workday, Greenhouse and Ashby.


**Price.** The builder, ATS score, keyword match, PDF and DOCX export are free, with no credit card. Simplify+ is $19.99 a week, $39.99 a month or $89.99 every 3 months, and adds AI rewriting, job-specific tailoring, AI chat and 100 Autopilot credits a week.


**Where others are better.** Simplify has four templates, all built for readability over design; Kickresume and Enhancv have far more visual choice. DOCX export works on the Classic, Accent and Minimalist layouts but not Modern. AI rewriting is paid, while Teal gives free users a few AI credits. And there's no lifetime plan like Rezi's.


Simplify is used by more than 2 million job seekers, and the Copilot extension is rated 4.8 out of 5 from about 3,900 reviews on the Chrome Web Store. In a 2022 survey of Harvard CS students it ranked among the top three places they found tech internships ([Harvard career center, archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20240228134502/https://careerservices.fas.harvard.edu/blog/2022/11/22/beyond-big-tech-where-can-i-find-summer-opportunities/) ), and the University of Washington's career center[recommends it](https://careers.uw.edu/resources/simplify/?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) for applying faster. I was named to the[Forbes 30 Under 30 2023](https://www.coca-colascholarsfoundation.org/blog/5-coke-scholars-named-brightest-young-entrepreneurs-leaders-and-stars-in-forbes-2023-30-under-30-list/?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) list for building Simplify, TechCrunch covered how[Simplify uses AI to help with job searches and applications](https://techcrunch.com/2024/02/07/simplify-looks-to-ai-to-help-with-job-searches-and-applications/?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) , and we're a[Y Combinator company](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/simplify?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) .


**Your next step:** open the resume builder, paste the description of the next job you're applying to, and add the missing skills you actually have before you hit export.


## 2. Teal: best for a resume and job tracker together


Teal is the closest thing to Simplify on this list, and the one I'd point you to if you mainly want a tidy place to manage a search. Its free plan is generous: unlimited resumes, 10 templates and unlimited job tracking.


**Tailoring.** Paste a job description and Teal highlights the keywords the posting cares about. Free users see the top 5. Teal+ shows every keyword plus a match score, so you can tell when a version is close enough to send. Free users also get a few AI credits: 5 for bullets, and 2 each for summaries and cover letters. That's enough to try the AI writing before you pay for it, which Simplify doesn't offer.


**Price.** Teal+ is $13 every 7 days, $29 every 30 days or $79 every 90 days, and it adds unlimited AI writing.


**Where it falls short.** Teal's help center says PDF is the only export format, so you'll need another tool when an application asks for a Word file. Teal also doesn't fill out or submit applications, so the applying is still on you.


## 3. Rezi: best for a one-time price


Rezi is built for ATS-first resumes, and it does the keyword work more carefully than most. AI Keyword Targeting reads a job description and lists the keywords you're missing. Then it asks whether each one actually fits your experience before working it in, which keeps you from claiming skills you don't have. The Rezi Score grades the resume in four areas (content, format, optimization and best practices), so you know which part to fix first.


Rezi has also grown past the resume itself. There's a cover letter generator that drafts from your resume, a chat-style AI agent for edits, and AI interview practice. Templates include the plain layouts recruiters in tech are used to, like Harvard and Jake's.


**Price.** The free plan is tight: 1 resume and 3 PDF downloads. Paid plans are $29 a month, $57 a quarter or $149 once for lifetime access. Exports include PDF, DOCX and Google Drive, the widest here. If you'll be job hunting on and off for years, the lifetime plan is good value. Rezi is rated 4.6 out of 5 on Trustpilot from 277 reviews.


**Where it falls short.** There's no job tracker and no autofill, so you'll pair it with something that handles the applying.


## 4. Jobscan: best for checking a resume against one job


Jobscan made its name on the match report, and it's still the most detailed one here. Upload a resume and a job description and it scores the fit across hard skills, soft skills, job title and education, then lists exactly what's missing. If you want to know why a resume isn't landing for a specific role, start here.


Its resume builder is now free too. It has one-column templates and an ATS badge on each section that tells you as you write whether a system can read it. You can import from LinkedIn, and PDF and Word downloads are free. A free account also includes 5 scans a month, a job tracker and a Chrome extension. AI Optimize rewrites your resume for a posting and adds missing keywords in a click. It needs Premium or a free trial. Jobscan also has a cover letter generator and AI interview practice that gives feedback on pace and filler words.


**Price.** Jobscan's plan prices are behind a sign-in, so I haven't listed them.


**One caution.** Don't chase a 100% match. A resume stuffed with keywords reads worse to the person who opens it, and our guide to[writing an ATS-friendly resume](https://simplify.jobs/blog/how-to-write-ats-resume-2026?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) covers how many keywords is enough.


## 5. Kickresume: best for design and career changers


Kickresume has the most template variety here, with 4 free templates and 40 more on Premium, plus matching cover letter templates so your application looks like one set. Its AI Writer drafts a resume from your target job title and the job ad. That's useful when you're moving fields and need your experience in a new industry's language. It also has a large library of pre-written phrases by job title, which helps when you're staring at an empty bullet. You can start from a LinkedIn import, and the same account includes an AI cover letter builder and an interview-question generator.


**Price.** Regular prices are $24 a month, $18 a month billed quarterly ($54) or $8 a month billed yearly ($96). Students with ISIC, ITIC or UNiDAYS status can get it free, which makes it the best deal here for many students. Kickresume is rated 4.7 out of 5 on Google.


**Where it falls short.** Downloads are unlimited, but its help center notes that Word exports are plain text, so the design only survives as a PDF. The ATS Resume Checker is a Premium feature.


## 6. Enhancv: best for polished one-page designs


Enhancv is for people who care how the page looks: many layouts, custom sections and fine design control. It's also more thoughtful about content than most design-first tools. Paste a job ad and pick three to five qualifications, and it tailors the resume around them. A match score highlights the terms you're missing. As you type, Improve Text suggests stronger wording. When a bullet needs a number, it leaves a placeholder instead of inventing one, which I'd like to see more tools do. You can build a first draft from your public LinkedIn URL, and there's a job tracker with a Chrome extension.


**Price.** The free plan lasts 7 days, adds Enhancv branding and caps each resume at 12 section items, so plan on paying if you use it. Paid plans are $39 a month, $69 a quarter or $99 for 6 months. Enhancv is rated 4.5 out of 5 from about 5,400 reviews on Reviews.io.


**Where it falls short.** Export is PDF, and the free plan is really a trial.


## 7. Resume.io: best for a fast first resume


Resume.io is the quickest way from nothing to a finished resume. Paste a job link and it pre-builds a resume to match the posting. Paste the same link and it writes a matching cover letter from your resume. You can even talk through your experience into the mic and let the AI clean it up. The templates are clean and labeled for ATS, and there's interview practice with instant feedback once you're further along.


**Price.** The free plan gives you one resume and one cover letter, downloadable only as plain text, so in practice it's paid. It costs $2.95 for a 7-day trial that renews at $29.95 every 4 weeks, or $49.95 a quarter, and Premium includes unlimited PDF downloads. Resume.io is rated 4.2 out of 5 from about 56,000 reviews on Trustpilot.


**Where it falls short.** The trial renews automatically, so cancel it if you only need one resume. Its pricing page doesn't say whether the AI tailoring rewrites your bullets or only picks a layout, so check before you pay.


## 8. ChatGPT: best free DIY option


A general AI assistant does much of what paid builders charge for if you do the setup. Paste a job description and one section of your resume and ask for the three biggest gaps, or ask it to rewrite a bullet to lead with a result. ChatGPT's free plan is enough for this; Go is $8 a month, Plus $20 and Pro from $100. What it won't do is lay out an ATS-friendly file, keep versions or track where you sent them, and it will invent numbers if you let it. Our guide to[using ChatGPT to improve your resume](https://simplify.jobs/blog/how-to-use-chatgpt-to-write-and-improve-your-resume?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) has prompts that keep it honest.


## Do AI resume builders get past ATS?


Usually, yes, as long as the template is simple. Jobscan's 2026 review found an applicant tracking system at[97.4% of Fortune 500 companies](https://www.jobscan.co/blog/fortune-500-use-applicant-tracking-systems/?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) , with Workday used by over 40% of them. These systems parse text, so a single-column layout, standard section names and consistent dates are what count. Every builder above can produce that.


AI-written content is a different question. In a[Canva survey of 5,000 job seekers](https://foxbusiness.com/technology/nearly-half-job-seekers-use-ai-polish-resumes?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) in eight countries, published in January 2024, about 45% said they had used generative AI to build, update or improve a resume. Our recruiter Ally explains[what gives an AI-written resume away](https://simplify.jobs/blog/can-recruiters-tell-if-ai-wrote-your-resume?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) : mostly generic bullets with no real numbers.


## Which AI resume builder should you use?


Pick by what's slowing you down:


If you need... Start with


A tailored resume for every application, free Simplify


A resume builder and tracker, with some free AI Teal or Simplify


A one-time payment Rezi lifetime


A strict match score for one posting Jobscan


Lots of design choice Kickresume or Enhancv


No new account at all ChatGPT


One tool is usually enough. Whichever you pick, keep a base resume and save a tailored copy for each job, then set a follow-up date for that application so it doesn't go quiet.


## Common questions


**What is the best AI resume builder?** For most job seekers, Simplify, because the builder, ATS score and keyword match are free and the tailored version goes straight into your applications and tracker. Rezi is better if you want to pay once, and Kickresume if design matters most.


**Is there a free AI resume builder?** Yes. Simplify's builder is free with PDF and DOCX export and an ATS score, and AI rewriting is part of Simplify+. Teal's free plan includes a handful of AI credits, and Jobscan's builder is free with 5 scans a month. ChatGPT is free if you're fine formatting the file yourself.


**Can ChatGPT build a resume?** It can write and edit the content, especially bullets and summaries tailored to a job description. It can't produce a formatted, ATS-friendly file or keep track of versions, so paste its output into a builder and check every claim.


**Is Teal or Rezi better?** Teal is better if you want a job tracker next to your resume and a usable free plan. Rezi is better if you want Word and Google Drive exports or a $149 lifetime plan.


**Are AI resume builders ATS friendly?** Most are, as long as you pick a simple single-column template with standard headings. The bigger risk is the content: keyword stuffing and invented achievements hurt you with the person reading it, even if the software parses the file fine.
